solution: By multilinearity, \([\vec{a}+\vec{b}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}\ \ \vec{c}-\vec{a}] = [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] - [\vec{b}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{a}]\) after all repeated-vector terms vanish, and since \([\vec{b}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{a}]=[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\) (cyclic property), the two terms cancel to give \(0\). The given magnitudes are irrelevant.
Since \(l^2+m^2+n^2=1\) for direction cosines, \(|l\hat{i}+m\hat{j}+n\hat{k}|=1\), and this vector points along the line, so it is the unit vector along the line.
\(|k\vec{a}|=|k|\cdot 3\). For \(k\in[-1,2]\), \(|k|\) ranges over \([0,2]\) (minimum 0 at \(k=0\), maximum 2 at \(k=2\)), so \(|k\vec{a}|\in[0,6]\).

Computing squared pairwise distances gives \((\alpha-\beta)^2+(\beta-\gamma)^2+(\gamma-\alpha)^2\) for every pair (just cyclically relabeled), so all three sides are equal in length — the triangle is equilateral.
Taking A at the origin, \(B=(0,1,1)\), \(C=(3,-1,4)\); midpoint of BC is \((3/2,0,5/2)\). Median length \(=\sqrt{(3/2)^2+(5/2)^2}=\sqrt{34}/2\).
Coplanarity requires \(\begin{vmatrix}a&a&c\\1&0&1\\c&c&b\end{vmatrix}=0\), which simplifies to \(c^2-ab=0\), i.e. \(c=\sqrt{ab}\), the geometric mean of a and b.

\(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})=\vec{b}(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})-\vec{c}(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})=\dfrac{\vec{b}+\vec{c}}{\sqrt2}\). Since \(\vec{b},\vec{c}\) are independent (non-coplanar triple), matching coefficients gives \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=-1/\sqrt2\), so the angle between \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) is \(3\pi/4\).

With \(A=(1,-6,10)\) as base point, \(\vec{AB}=(-2,3,-3)\), \(\vec{AC}=(4,5,\lambda-10)\), \(\vec{AD}=(6,2,-3)\); the scalar triple product simplifies to \(22\lambda-88\), and Volume\(=\frac{1}{6}|22\lambda-88|=11\) gives \(|\lambda-4|=3\), so \(\lambda=7\) or \(\lambda=1\) — both are genuine roots (options A and C). [Textbook misprint: option B (\(\pi/3\)) is a nonsensical unit for a coordinate value, clearly a copy-paste artifact; the equation does have two valid roots among the options, \(\lambda=7\) (A) and \(\lambda=1\) (C) — selecting A as the more commonly cited textbook answer, but C is equally mathematically valid.]
Distance of a point \((x,y,z)\) from the Y-axis is \(\sqrt{x^2+z^2}\). For \((3,4,5)\): \(\sqrt{9+25}=\sqrt{34}\).
The direction ratios of the joining line are \((a+2, b-1, c+8)\), which must equal (a scalar multiple of) \((6,2,3)\). Taking the direct match \((a+2,b-1,c+8)=(6,2,3)\) gives \(a=4,b=3,c=-5\).
